name: Willoughby Corner Phase IB Family Apartments
award: 2022 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Willoughby Corner Phase IB is 129 all-electric, zero-energy-ready family apartments (four buildings) at or below 60% AMI in Boulder County Housing Authority's 400-home Willoughby Corner neighborhood in Lafayette; BCHA won 2022 Round Two federal 4% and $1M state credits, and the phase was complete, fully leased and placed in service by November 2025.
why_it_matters: It is the bond-financed half of the 192-home first phase (paired with a 9% senior building), built on land Lafayette bought and with half the water rights paid by the city, and it set aside a preference for income-qualified Marshall Fire survivors.

status.label: Completed, fully leased, placed in service (November 2025)
status.detail: BCHA's 2026 CHFA application for Phase 2A says the first phase, including the 129 family apartments, was fully leased and placed in service in November 2025; Phase 1 held its grand opening on 2025-08-21. No 8609 record was found.

next_step: Watch for 8609 issuance and for Phase 2A (32 IDD homes), which won 2026 Round One credits.

key_numbers.meaning: 87 one-bedroom, 30 two-bedroom and 12 three-bedroom apartments for families at or below 60% AMI.
Plus $1,000,000 of state credit; BCHA itself issued $33,250,000 in tax-exempt bonds.
7 units at 30%, 9 at 40%, 52 at 50% and 61 at 60% AMI.
Bond counsel's figure for the Series 2023 Willoughby Corner Multifamily bonds; it does not say which buildings it covers.

facts.value: N. 120th Street and E. Emma Street, Lafayette, CO 80026

Two three-story apartment buildings with elevators and two two-story nine-unit flats, plus a one-story community building; named Bluestem Place, Sugar Beet House, Peach Tree House and Purple Prairie Place
All-electric, geothermal heating and cooling, rooftop and ground-mounted solar; Zero Energy Ready Homes certification target
Part of a 24-acre site in a qualified census tract (608.00), zoned R-4 high-density residential with a PUD overlay
RTD DASH and 225D service extended to the neighborhood; residents get a free RTD Eco-Pass
One-bedroom 60% AMI units listed at $1,642 a month including all utilities; all 30%, 40% and 50% AMI units leased
Not project-based Section 8; Housing Choice Voucher holders may apply

money.note: Annual credit, runs 10 years. Federal credit investor: Hudson Housing Capital.
State credit investor: Monarch Private Capital.

Application: private placement, $15,400,000 permanent bonds and about $6,600,000 taxable construction loan. Bond counsel later described Series 2023 bonds of up to $37,791,108. BCHA as issuer implies BCHA's own or assigned bond cap (inferred).

money.source: Other gap sources named in the application
money.note: Colorado Division of Housing soft funds, Boulder County Worthy Cause funds, BCHA gap funding and deferred developer fee.

money.source: City of Lafayette land, water and fees (whole neighborhood)
money.amount: $3.1M-$3.5M land, half of water rights, about $1.5M fee waivers
money.note: Water rights for the site received $5.3M in grants; Boulder County added nearly $13M of county and ARPA money across the first phase.

parties.role: Sponsor (as CHFA prints it), developer, bond issuer, owner and manager
parties.name: Boulder County Housing Authority (BCHA)
Pinkard Construction (named for preconstruction by BCHA and as builder in the topping-out report)

background.text: Lafayette, Boulder County and BCHA control the 24-acre site under an intergovernmental agreement that dedicates the land to permanently affordable housing; the city bought the land and assigned it to BCHA.
Phase 1A (63 apartments for adults 55+, now Búho Place) won 9% credits in May 2022; Phase 1B is the 4% family half of Phase 1, and BCHA planned to close both together.
Lafayette rezoned the site to R-4 in April 2022 and the Planning Commission approved the PUD overlay 6-0; the final PUD was recorded on 2022-11-30.
Lafayette City Council unanimously approved BCHA's site plan for the first phase on 2023-04-18.
CHFA's award description says BCHA will give a preference to income-qualified residents displaced by the December 2021 Marshall Fire.
Each phase repays BCHA its share of site infrastructure (Phase 1B: 129 of 400 homes, 32.25%); the first phase included about $15M in infrastructure.
The application targeted a January 2023 closing; Boulder County later expected first-phase loans to close in early May 2023, and bond counsel announced the Series 2023 bonds on 2023-05-22.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award report lists $33,250,000 of BCHA bonds, while bond counsel describes the Series 2023 Willoughby Corner Multifamily bonds as up to $37,791,108.

Bond counsel puts total project cost at about $73.5 million; the topping-out report's headline says $80 million and its text says total development and construction costs are $114 million, likely for different scopes.
The narrative says Lafayette paid $3.5 million for the land, while Boulder County's April 2023 release says $3.1 million.

open_questions: Exact financial closing date and the split of the bonds and costs between the family phase and the senior building.
